title: fix(qa): keep Telegram round-trip checks on the exercised route
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137139

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Telegram round-trip checks being rejected or sent to the wrong conversation after a selected direct-message, channel, or forum-topic scenario.

## User Impact

QA operators can repeat latency checks on the conversation and topic actually exercised by the selected scenario, using the provisioned primary participant. There is no change to normal Telegram chat behavior or credential handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the QA bus cursor before each scenario attempt and resolve the probe route from that attempt's surviving inbound or outbound messages for the active account. This covers scenarios without a single declared conversation, including outbound-only flows, without parsing scenario actions or maintaining another route catalog.

The first probe is fresh; later probes reply only to their own preceding responses. A response from another topic fails the probe instead of counting as a latency sample. Explicit-input probes remain supported, and native observer admission guards are unchanged.

This reworks Vincent Koc's original PR against the current QA lifecycle while preserving its branch and history. The original stays open until this canonical replacement is verified merged.

## Evidence

- Remote real-adapter boundary proof: the original runner/probe produced three intended native admission failures for direct-message, channel, and forum routes; the repaired runner passed all three. The full adapter test file passed 19 tests. Only the credential/userbot edge is mocked; no authenticated Telegram message was sent.
- Round-trip unit proof covers route selection, stale/deleted/foreign-account observations, reply chaining, and failure budgets. A negative control without the topic check failed its regression for the intended reason.
- Current-main exact-head focused proof at `21e618b9926`: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/adapter.runtime.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-round-trip.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-run-standard.parity-retry.test.ts test/scripts/npm-telegram-live.test.ts` — 4 files, 98/98 passed in 40.08 s wall.
- Current-main complete changed-surface gate at `21e618b9926`: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — green across formatting, architecture/dependency guards, extension + extension-test + script + root-test typechecks, dead-code scans, affected lint, database-first guard, and import-cycle checks.
- Fresh independent Sol/high AutoReview at `21e618b9926`: scoped-clean through P1, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Earlier source-pinned remote proof: [run 36281998699](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36281998699) returned exit 0 with the fixture removed, source restored, transport unchanged, and lease completed. A cancelled backing Actions step represents one-shot Testbox cleanup, not a failed application result.
- Earlier exact-head PR CI [36282766913](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36282766913) completed successfully at `7b1bfce0ef6`: 40 jobs passed and 22 skipped. Fresh exact-head CI for the mechanical current-main rebase is required before landing.

### Test Cost

Current-main combined single-worker command wall time is 40.08 s for the four changed test files above, including runner preparation/import overhead.

Exact-head CI [36357551987](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36357551987) reports:

- `test/scripts/npm-telegram-live.test.ts` ran alone in `core-tooling-7-hosted-2`: 48/48 passed, 1.61 s Vitest duration, 2.41 s wrapper wall.
- The three changed extension test files ran in `changed-extensions-config`: 36/36 files passed, 107.03 s Vitest duration, 109.44 s wrapper wall for the complete extension shard.
- The extension shard emits per-test-case milliseconds and one aggregate shard duration, not per-file wall times. Therefore exact per-file CI seconds are unavailable for those three files; the source-pinned single-worker per-file measurements below are the applicable per-file costs.

Retained source-pinned per-file wall times from the prior clean head:

| Test File | Passed | Wall Time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/adapter.runtime.test.ts` | 19 | 2.479 s |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-round-trip.test.ts` | 8 | 1.514 s |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-run-standard.parity-retry.test.ts` | 23 | 28.713 s |
| `test/scripts/npm-telegram-live.test.ts` | 48 | 2.532 s |

These are command wall times, not isolated case durations or a claim of CI speedup.

### Review Disposition

The [completed ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159284#issuecomment-5851336537) found no actionable code findings. Its test-cost request is addressed above. The only post-review change is a conflict-free mechanical rebase onto current `main`; behavior and the eight-file diff are unchanged.

Maintainer disposition: accept the retained boundary proof for this internal QA routing change, with authenticated Test Server validation recorded as an unrun follow-up rather than a claimed pass. The repair changes the runner-to-adapter handoff, not Telegram's API, credential leasing, native admission, or userbot wire behavior. The actual runner factory and adapter were exercised for direct, channel, and forum routes, including native destination/topic IDs and reply chaining; restoring the original handoff produced the three intended admission failures. Only the existing credential/userbot edge is mocked. Exact-head required CI, enforced reviews, and native landing checks are not waived.
